summary: joule-btp-extension 0.1.6 executes install-time reverse shell and exfiltrates host data
details: setup.py runs an install-time payload gated on the PIP_BUILD_TRACKER/PIP_REQ_TRACKER environment variables set by pip. When triggered, it double-forks a daemon that opens a TCP socket to a hardcoded host:port (127.0.0.1:4444 in this build) and executes commands received over the socket via subprocess.run(shell=True), returning stdout/stderr back over the socket — a fully structured reverse shell. In parallel, it collects the installer's hostname, a selected set of environment variables (HOME, USER, LOGNAME, VIRTUAL_ENV, PATH, PIP_CACHE_DIR, npm_config_prefix, GIT_EDITOR), reads /etc/passwd and /etc/hosts, walks the current working directory and VIRTUAL_ENV reading file contents (up to 4 KB per file, <=32 KB total), and POSTs a JSON report to a hardcoded https://42b1-2a02-2ad0-103-2841-51cc-a5b3-6bc2-68fe.ngrok-free.app/asd endpoint, followed by a second POST of /etc/passwd bytes. The package docstring self-describes as a supply-chain proof-of-concept targeting the SAP Joule Desktop sandbox, but the shipped code is a fully functional install-time backdoor plus data exfiltrator that fires on any `pip install` of this version.
